title: A few latch units make state-space models generalize over horizon.
rationale: This is a crisp architectural hypothesis grounded in a specific theoretical deficiency, with dramatic controlled extrapolation and strong representation-learning relevance. It needs comparisons to modern gated SSMs and ablations showing true bistability, not extra parameters, drives gains.
compute_data_notes: Synthetic POMDP memory tasks require no external data and tiny models can sweep horizons, seeds, latch counts, and baselines rapidly on one 3080.

title: RL gain as a function of pretraining exposure.
rationale: An unusually clean controlled answer to a central RLVR capability debate, with a strong non-monotonic prediction and no proprietary-data ambiguity; external validity from 20–100M synthetic models is the chief weakness.
compute_data_notes: All corpora and labels are procedurally generated, so data access is excellent; dozens of pretraining/RLVR runs are compute-heavy but 20–100M models can fit 10 GB over two to three weeks with optimized code.

title: Emergent quasimetric structure in goal-conditioned critics.
rationale: This combines a strong structural measurement, a predictive diagnostic for stitching, and a lightweight regularizer against specialized architectures. It is well aligned with representation learning and goal-conditioned RL; careful sign/discount transformations and valid triangle definitions are essential.
compute_data_notes: OGBench and maze tasks are public, small, and offline-friendly. Triple sampling and comparison to one quasimetric architecture are feasible on a 3080 in one to two weeks.

title: Sobolev critics from differentiable simulators.
rationale: High methodological novelty, a principled use of differentiable simulation, and strong gradient-quality diagnostics make this top-tier if contact robustness holds; adjacent Sobolev/value-gradient work must be ruled out.
compute_data_notes: MJX/Brax are public and fit a 3080, but simulator Jacobians and second-order effects can be memory-intensive; a focused two-week study is plausible with careful batching.

title: Does RL create new behaviors in interactive environments, or only sharpen them?
rationale: This directly tests a high-impact claim in a setting where exploration changes the conceptual answer. Trajectory support is hard to establish from finite samples, but careful coverage estimators and interactive controls could make it exceptional.
compute_data_notes: BabyAI-text and TextWorld are public and environment execution is cheap. Training 0.5–1B models and sampling pass@k up to 256 is generation-heavy but feasible with a focused task suite.

title: Two kinds of sparsity: rarity versus distance.
rationale: A crisp conceptual decomposition, controllable 2D benchmark, and clear method-by-axis predictions could correct common evaluation claims; strength depends on showing the taxonomy explains established benchmarks, not only synthetic tasks.
compute_data_notes: Procedural gridworld and MinAtar generators use public code and tiny models; broad methods and seeds remain easily manageable on one 3080 in two weeks.

title: The out-of-span penalty for pretrained skills.
rationale: Mapping negative transfer and predicting its sign before fine-tuning addresses a real weakness in skill discovery. The key difficulty is defining a meaningful, computable skill span for nonlinear policies; if the statistic is post hoc, the central claim weakens substantially.
compute_data_notes: DMC, mazes, DIAYN, and METRA implementations are public. Pretraining multiple skill sets plus downstream grids is run-heavy but feasible on one GPU with a narrow suite in about two weeks.

title: The Baldwin effect in meta-RL.
rationale: A controlled stable/varying split yields a clean demonstration of assimilation dynamics and a strong OOD-adaptability trade-off. The concept is classic, so top-tier strength depends on discovering a general law rather than merely illustrating the Baldwin effect in tiny tasks.
compute_data_notes: Procedural bandits and gridworlds are tiny and can be generated publicly. RL2 and small transformers, checkpoint ablations, and many seeds are easily feasible on one 3080.

title: Rewarding lucky guesses.
rationale: Strong causal hypothesis, exact procedural process labels, and a practical filtering intervention address a major outcome-reward weakness; defining wrong reasoning robustly across generated traces is the main challenge.
compute_data_notes: Synthetic arithmetic/graph/logic data and checkers avoid proprietary dependencies; 0.5–1B LoRA GRPO is feasible on 10 GB but rollout generation likely takes one to two weeks.

title: Counterfactual token importance as the credit signal.
rationale: Direct intervention for token credit is methodologically interesting, falsifiable, and closely aligned with current reasoning-model research. Re-sampling after many span deletions is expensive and high-variance, while token-level weighting under sequence-level policy gradients needs careful derivation to avoid bias.
compute_data_notes: Synthetic tasks and 0.5B models are public, but counterfactual generations multiply rollout cost by spans per answer. A small proof of concept fits one 3080; a robust multi-domain comparison may exceed a reasonable two-week budget.

title: A validation set for RL: cross-fitted Bellman error.
rationale: RL model selection without environment evaluation is a major problem, and cross-fitting offers a clean methodological proposal with measurable calibration. The idea must confront known Bellman-error identifiability failures; cross-fitting removes overfitting but not inherent proxy mismatch.
compute_data_notes: Public offline datasets and small online benchmarks suffice. Two critics roughly double training cost but remain easy on one 3080, and true-value estimates can be obtained in small simulators.

title: State coverage versus action coverage in offline RL.
rationale: Separating two conflated coverage axes and producing a method-selection map is foundational, falsifiable, and broadly useful. The hard part is constructing genuinely independent axes in continuous domains and defining robust summary statistics rather than benchmark-specific controls.
compute_data_notes: MuJoCo and maze generators are public and offline training is inexpensive. Generating a dense 2D grid for five methods is run-heavy but feasible in roughly two weeks on a 3080 with small networks.

title: Answer-mode collapse on multi-solution problems.
rationale: This identifies a hidden failure mode that standard single-answer RLVR benchmarks cannot reveal and offers a targeted diversity objective. It is timely and empirically clear, though coverage rewards require enumerability and may encourage superficial variants rather than semantically distinct solutions.
compute_data_notes: Enumerable procedural tasks and 0.5B-1B public models keep evaluation clean. GRPO runs and solution canonicalization are feasible on one 3080 in roughly one to two weeks.

title: Is hierarchy just long credit?
rationale: A decisive matched-credit audit could materially change interpretation of hierarchical RL results and has excellent falsifiability. Novelty is at risk if prior HRL studies include similar controls, and faithfully reproducing several hierarchy methods makes execution much harder than the proposal suggests.
compute_data_notes: Craftax and AntMaze-like environments are public, but implementing and tuning several HRL baselines plus matched flat agents is substantial. One 3080 can support a focused benchmark set in two to four weeks, not an exhaustive audit.

title: Does RLVR compose?
rationale: Composition is a high-value, falsifiable generalization test with well-controlled skills and training-order comparisons; constructing genuinely compositional tasks without shortcuts is difficult but decisive.
compute_data_notes: Data and exact checkers can be generated publicly; multiple 0.5–1B training regimes and held-out compositions are feasible with LoRA on 10 GB in around two weeks, though tight.

title: Structured label noise in preference learning.
rationale: Difficulty-dependent annotator noise is realistic, mathematically tractable, and linked to downstream control rather than reward-model fit alone. Identifiability between reward gap and noise is the major issue, and validation on public preferences may lack ground truth, but a principled estimator could be strong.
compute_data_notes: Simulated preference labels on public control tasks are cheap, and several public preference datasets can provide qualitative validation. Reward fitting and downstream RL are manageable on one 3080 in one to two weeks.

title: Correlated exploration noise is a hidden coordination channel.
rationale: Surprising, sharply falsifiable, and directly relevant to MARL reproducibility and zero-shot coordination; reviewers may question prevalence unless real implementations are audited in addition to controlled injections.
compute_data_notes: JaxMARL is public and lightweight; noise-stream interventions, cross-play, and many seeds are readily feasible on a single 3080 in a week.

title: Ground-truth action gradients expose the actor exploiting the critic.
rationale: An unusually direct measurement of a central deep-RL failure story, with causal interventions and informative negative outcomes. Finite-difference gradients are only ground truth up to rollout horizon and stochastic noise, so estimator validation is crucial.
compute_data_notes: Cloneable DMC-like simulators and algorithms are public. Per-action-dimension branched rollouts are expensive but can be sampled sparsely at checkpoints; low-dimensional tasks make a strong study possible on one 3080.

title: Frequency response of the learner.
rationale: System identification gives a novel, rigorous lens, quantitative predictions, and a strong validation test from frequency response to step response. It is unusually broad if resonance predicts natural nonstationarity, though reviewers may demand theory and more than synthetic reward modulation.
compute_data_notes: MinAtar and selected DMC tasks are public; the main cost is frequency-by-hyperparameter sweeps. Small parallel environments make a convincing study feasible in two weeks with careful scope.

title: Anytime-valid comparisons of RL algorithms.
rationale: This addresses pervasive optional-stopping errors with established but underused statistical machinery, measurable compute savings, and a reusable tool. Novel statistical theory may be limited and prior sequential RL-evaluation work must be ruled out, but careful dependence and multiple-task treatment could make it broadly significant.
compute_data_notes: Gymnax/Craftax are public and tiny; large seed pools are feasible on a 3080 and can often reuse archived curves. Implementation and simulations should fit comfortably within a week.

title: Entropy conversion efficiency.
rationale: The conversion ratio is an appealing task property that could predict algorithm choice before training, giving the idea broad utility. State entropy estimation across heterogeneous spaces and random-policy dependence are serious definition issues; success requires a robust normalized estimator and held-out prediction.
compute_data_notes: Random rollouts and standard SAC/state-entropy baselines use public environments and modest compute. A multi-suite validation is feasible on one 3080 in one to two weeks.

title: The TD update is not a gradient. Measure its curl.
rationale: A crisp, falsifiable diagnostic tied to established theory and a concrete controller. It could be methodologically important if curl predicts failures beyond standard statistics, but novelty depends on careful separation from game-dynamics and Jacobian analyses.
compute_data_notes: MinAtar and DMC are public and small networks fit easily. Jacobian antisymmetry estimates add cost but randomized JVP/HVP estimators make a multi-seed study realistic on a 10 GB RTX 3080 in roughly two weeks.

title: Token-level credit assignment with ground-truth intermediate states.
rationale: This offers a rare controlled test of sequence credit assignment and a concrete method with oracle-free testing. It must distinguish denser supervision from better credit assignment and test whether benefits survive imperfect intermediate-state labels.
compute_data_notes: Counting and graph generators provide unlimited public labels. A 0.5B LoRA model, short traces, and sequence-versus-step baselines are feasible on one 3080.

title: Range compression in critics.
rationale: Focusing on calibration slope rather than overestimation intercept is sharp, potentially novel, and directly linked to rare-mode exploitation. The intervention is testable, but Monte Carlo targets in continuing tasks are noisy and post-hoc recalibration must avoid becoming an ad hoc fix.
compute_data_notes: Public DMC and Craftax data can be generated locally. Rollout-based ground truth adds cost but remains practical for small task sets and checkpoints on a 3080.

title: Buffer transplant: decomposing algorithm differences into exploration and learning.
rationale: A strong causal evaluation design addressing a central ambiguity in RL comparisons; cross-algorithm buffer compatibility and PPO/world-model inclusion complicate a clean decomposition.
compute_data_notes: DMC/Craftax are public; many paired branches and multiple algorithms cost roughly two 3080-weeks, with world-model agents the main memory risk.

title: Mutation testing for RL: which bugs can diagnostics catch?
rationale: A systematic mutation benchmark and minimal monitor set would be high-value infrastructure with immediate reproducibility impact. It is engineering-heavy and venue reviewers may question research novelty, so realistic mutations, false-positive control, and cross-implementation generalization matter.
compute_data_notes: CleanRL code and public environments eliminate data barriers. Thirty mutations times seeds is a large run matrix, but small PPO/SAC tasks make it feasible on one 3080 in about two weeks.

title: Does depth buy horizon generalization?
rationale: A direct mechanistic test of a prominent depth result with a quantitative invariance metric is compelling, especially for ICLR. Acceptance strength requires controls separating depth from parameter count, optimization, and effective receptive computation.
compute_data_notes: Point mazes and CRL are cheap and public, but 512-layer sweeps with multiple seeds can be slow and unstable on 10 GB. Manipulation should be limited to a small task set.

title: Exact counterfactual credit via cloning in cooperative MARL.
rationale: Exact counterfactual credit is a natural and significant use of cloneable simulators, with clear baselines and a diagnostic approximation gap. 'Exact Shapley-style' can become exponentially costly, so the paper must define tractable estimators and fair compute matching.
compute_data_notes: JaxMARL environments are public and GPU-friendly. One-agent action replacement is practical; full coalitional Shapley credit is not. A restricted exact-counterfactual study is feasible in roughly two weeks.

title: Tool-induced skill atrophy.
rationale: The deployment concern is concrete, the within-operation prediction is strong, and tool dropout is a simple remedy. It could be exceptional for AAAI if genuine atrophy is separated from changed prompting or policy routing and demonstrated beyond toy arithmetic.
compute_data_notes: Small public language models and generated arithmetic/graph data avoid proprietary dependencies. Tool-augmented GRPO on 0.5B-1B models is feasible on a 3080 with short contexts, though multiple checkpoints and no-tool evaluations take one to two weeks.

title: Prefix-only GRPO: how much of RLVR fits in a soft prompt?
rationale: Using trainable capacity as a measurement of elicitation versus learning is timely and especially well matched to ICLR. Prompt tuning with RL may have close concurrent work, and cross-size prefix transfer can be architecture/tokenizer-sensitive; merely recovering benchmark gains is not enough.
compute_data_notes: Public 0.5B models and procedural tasks are available. Prefix training is memory-light, but GRPO rollouts, LoRA/full-tuning comparisons, sizes, lengths, and seeds create substantial compute; a narrowed 0.5B-1B study is feasible on 10GB.

title: Durbin–Watson for TD: residual autocorrelation along trajectories.
rationale: Distinctive reuse of a classical diagnostic, a strong MDP-versus-POMDP prediction, and an actionable penalty make a coherent paper; whitening assumptions and policy-induced temporal dependence require careful controls.
compute_data_notes: POPGym, masked DMC, and small diagnostic tasks are public and cheap; extensive controls are feasible on one 3080 within a week.

title: When does pathwise beat score-function on-policy?
rationale: Estimator selection is a fundamental methodological question, and controlled task factors plus a switching rule create a strong complete story. Causal task construction and matched optimization effort are needed to avoid benchmark-specific conclusions.
compute_data_notes: Mujoco Playground is public and GPU-parallel, making broad sweeps unusually feasible on a 3080. REPPO and PPO implementations must be equally optimized and compute-accounted.

title: Trust regions on the state distribution, not the action distribution.
rationale: Methodologically substantial and tied to theory, with a potentially important replacement for action KL; density-ratio estimation, intervention design, and likely adjacent prior work create meaningful risk.
compute_data_notes: Public Playground and Procgen are available, but repeated rollouts plus classifier fitting and tuning raise cost; a focused task set is feasible in two weeks on 10 GB.

title: Model-tolerant actors.
rationale: This proposes a principled model-based objective with a clear error-sensitivity mechanism and a predicted domain-dependent trade-off. Lipschitz estimation/regularization may be loose, and convincing results require strong Dreamer/TD-MPC2 implementations and contact-rich counterexamples.
compute_data_notes: DMC is public, but DreamerV3 and TD-MPC2 sweeps are memory- and wall-clock-intensive on a 10GB 3080. A small-model, few-task paper is possible in two to three weeks; broad claims are risky.

title: Partner identification time predicts zero-shot coordination.
rationale: The temporal diagnostic is crisp, representation-focused, and directly tied to zero-shot coordination, while the auxiliary provides a falsifiable improvement. Partner labels and probe accuracy may not reflect convention-relevant inference, so causal evidence and diverse held-out partners are important.
compute_data_notes: Overcooked and small Hanabi implementations are public and modest in size. Population training multiplies runs but remains practical on one GPU in about two weeks.

title: Do recurrent policies represent uncertainty or just the mode?
rationale: Excellent controlled POMDP question connecting probes, Bayes beliefs, failures, and an intervention; probe non-recoverability does not prove absent information, so nonlinear and causal controls are essential.
compute_data_notes: All proposed belief-computable environments can be generated publicly and are tiny; GRU/Transformer agents fit comfortably and require days, not large compute.

title: Depth helps self-supervised RL. Does it help bootstrapped RL, and if not, why?
rationale: A timely, falsifiable limit study with a strong mechanistic angle and excellent ICLR fit. Competitiveness depends on going beyond depth curves to a convincing explanation and remedy; the proposed breadth is aggressive.
compute_data_notes: DMC is public, but 2-to-256-layer sweeps, multiple algorithms, seeds, diagnostics, and HumanoidBench are unlikely to finish credibly in mere days on a 10 GB 3080. A narrowed DMC-only study is feasible.

title: A mechanistic decomposition of frame skip.
rationale: Frame skip is ubiquitous, and a controlled decomposition plus a task-level predictor could have broad practical significance. The key risk is imperfect separability and confounding among discount, update count, and temporal abstraction; a formal causal design would materially strengthen it.
compute_data_notes: DMC, MinAtar, and Playground-style simulators are public and inexpensive. The variants require engineering but no large models, making a strong multi-task study feasible in one to two weeks.

title: How fast does a policy identify its own latency?
rationale: Identification time is a precise representation-level quantity linked to a dynamical task timescale, and the auxiliary gives an actionable intervention. Linear-probe recoverability does not prove online use, so causal hidden-state interventions or controlled probes would strengthen the claim.
compute_data_notes: Latency randomization, recurrent policies, and probes are inexpensive in public DMC/Playground environments. The full sweep is feasible within two weeks on one GPU.

title: Action parameterization sets the color of exploration.
rationale: The unification of absolute, delta, and filtered actions through spectral exploration is compelling, and the plant-bandwidth predictor elevates it above an ablation paper. Estimating bandwidth robustly in nonlinear contact systems and separating exploration from policy-class effects are the central risks.
compute_data_notes: DMC and MyoSuite are public; parameterization variants are cheap. Multiple control frequencies and spectral analyses are feasible on one GPU in one to two weeks.

title: The deadly triad has high-leverage transitions.
rationale: Leverage gives a distinctive, testable account of deep-TD instability and a simple intervention. Strong upside, though approximate eNTK leverage may be noisy and the causal claim requires more than correlation on toy divergence cases.
compute_data_notes: Baird tasks, DMC, and Atari data are public. Random-projection NTK features and buffer-wide estimation may be memory and runtime heavy, so a carefully chosen Atari-100k subset is necessary on 10 GB.

title: Does IRL recover the reward or the shaping?
rationale: This connects a known identifiability theorem to a concrete modern failure mode and dynamics-transfer test, with strong scientific value even under a negative result. The decomposition must be defined rigorously, and three competitive IRL implementations make execution demanding.
compute_data_notes: Synthetic known-reward MuJoCo tasks avoid private data, but AIRL, IQ-Learn, diffusion IRL, demonstrations, and dynamics-shift evaluations may require a tightly scoped two-week study.

title: Offline RL with the behavior policy known.
rationale: An oracle behavior-policy comparison cleanly decomposes estimation from value-learning error and could redirect offline-RL effort. Some listed methods do not consume an explicit behavior density, so the intervention must be method-faithful; synthetic D4RL-style data also limits direct benchmark relevance.
compute_data_notes: Known policies can generate public MuJoCo datasets locally, and offline methods are 3080-friendly. Multiple methods and mixture types remain manageable in one to two weeks.

title: Wrapper sensitivity: how much do environment conventions move the leaderboard?
rationale: High reproducibility value, strong effect-size framing, and immediate community relevance; factorial auditing is less methodologically novel and must avoid overstating results from only two algorithms or suites.
compute_data_notes: DMC and Gymnasium MuJoCo are public; a fractional factorial with enough seeds is compute-intensive but straightforward on a 3080 over one to two weeks.

title: Hyperparameter drift measured by forking.
rationale: A direct and compelling way to measure nonstationary optima and derive schedules, with held-out validation; short-horizon branch winners may be myopic and the branching budget is large.
compute_data_notes: Public Playground supports cheap parallel forks, but checkpoints times branches times three hyperparameters substantially multiply compute; a focused two-week 3080 study is plausible.

title: The empirical contraction modulus of deep fitted Q-iteration.
rationale: Strong bridge from classical theory to deep-RL stability with a predictive claim; measurement validity is the main risk because the fitted projection and sampled norm can make the modulus estimator ambiguous.
compute_data_notes: Public control suites suffice, but repeated critic perturbations and fitting rounds multiply training cost; feasible on a 3080 in roughly two weeks with small nets.

title: Domain randomization at replay time via re-simulation.
rationale: A novel, useful augmentation enabled by cloneable simulation with strong robustness and nominal-performance tests; validity is limited when altered physics makes stored states inconsistent or unreachable.
compute_data_notes: MJX/Playground are public, but robust save/restore and physics perturbation infrastructure is nontrivial; feasible in two weeks if the simulator supports batched cloning.

title: Dimensionless hyperparameters.
rationale: A successful invariance law would be broadly significant and methodologically elegant, especially for ICML. The proposal is currently under-specified about units and dimensionless groups, and exhaustive optimization across rescaled families may reveal only known normalization effects.
compute_data_notes: Public simulators suffice, but reliable optimum estimation across reward, timestep, horizon, and action-dimension axes requires many sweeps. It is possible on a 3080 only with small tasks and disciplined experimental design.

title: Stratified evaluation: cut evaluation cost by sampling where policies disagree.
rationale: Practical evaluation methodology with a crisp ranking-fidelity objective and large claimed savings; unbiased estimators and the cost of discovering disagreement strata must be included for a fair comparison.
compute_data_notes: Only trained policies and public simulators are needed; evaluation is cheap, data access is unrestricted, and days on a 3080 are sufficient.

title: The recovery paradox.
rationale: This is a strong, counterintuitive application insight with a clean exposure-mediated mechanism and direct robustness implications. It is less methodologically novel for ICML, but could be excellent if interventions establish causality rather than a simple shaping trade-off.
compute_data_notes: Public GPU locomotion simulators provide all data and perturbations. Quadruped studies are easy; humanoid breadth and sufficient seeds remain feasible but should be scoped carefully.

title: Does self-play rotate or converge? Measuring the Hamiltonian component.
rationale: Strong theory-to-deep-learning bridge with a measurable quantity, exploitability target, and controller. The Jacobian estimator may not scale or distinguish local parameter rotation from strategically meaningful cycling, and recent prior work is a notable novelty risk.
compute_data_notes: Kuhn poker and small Overcooked variants are public and cheap. Game-Jacobian products and exploitability computation add engineering but fit on one 3080 with small policies.

title: The determinism assumption in default hyperparameters.
rationale: Stochasticity is a consequential neglected axis, and validated shift laws would offer practical defaults beyond another robustness benchmark. The hypothesized directions are not universally obvious, requiring substantial retuning and held-out validation to avoid post hoc trends.
compute_data_notes: Public simulators permit controlled dynamics and observation noise, but per-noise hyperparameter optimization across four knobs is expensive. A reduced factorial is feasible on one 3080 in two to three weeks.

title: A difficulty-mixing law for low-data RLVR.
rationale: A validated law across procedural domains and held-out transfer would be methodologically strong. The required grid and scale range may be too small to justify a law, while many RLVR runs make the claimed budget unrealistic.
compute_data_notes: Procedural data removes availability constraints, but mixing-fraction by budget by domain by seed for 0.5–1.5B models is expensive on a single 3080. Restricting to 0.5B and efficient inference is essential.

title: Solver–verifier asymmetry under RL.
rationale: The 2x2 transfer matrix is clean and extends a central frozen-model observation into training dynamics. Novelty is moderate and task construction must avoid verifier shortcuts; joint training and transfer claims need multiple domains and careful matched data.
compute_data_notes: Open 0.5B-1B models and generated domains suffice. Four training regimes across three domains are achievable but near the upper end of a one-3080, two-week budget.

title: Groups sampled without replacement.
rationale: A precise GRPO sampling improvement with clean small-group predictions and diagnostics, but sequence-level without-replacement sampling is technically underspecified and diverse decoding is a crowded area.
compute_data_notes: Synthetic tasks and public sub-billion models suffice; implementing unbiased or controlled stratified sequence sampling is harder than the compute, which otherwise fits one 3080-week.

title: Detecting spurious Q-optimism at fine-tune onset.
rationale: A measurable failure signal that gates updates is timely and offers causal validation. Reliance on a withdrawn anchor weakens framing, and defining truly worse actions or rank flips without ground-truth action values requires care.
compute_data_notes: D4RL and OGBench are public. AntMaze is manageable, while kitchen can be slow and high variance; three strong baselines and seeds make two weeks optimistic but credible on one 3080.

title: Answer-first RL: are reasoning tokens causal?
rationale: A provocative, decisive intervention on whether generated reasoning is causally useful during RL, with informative outcomes either way. Answer-first generation changes conditioning and training distribution, so it is not a perfectly isolated causal test and needs careful controls.
compute_data_notes: Procedural math and public QA data are available. A 0.5B LoRA experiment is possible in 10 GB, and only a few conditions are needed, though RL generation remains slow enough to constrain seeds.

title: Numerical precision is an RL hyperparameter.
rationale: The cancellation mechanism is precise, falsifiable, broadly consequential, and supports a nearly free remedy. Strong analytical predictions in gamma, reward scale, and Q magnitude would elevate it beyond a systems ablation.
compute_data_notes: DMC and MinAtar are public and inexpensive; fp16/bf16 support and logging require modest engineering, with days to roughly one week of 3080 compute.

title: Teacher cloneability.
rationale: Teacher selection by student learnability is practically valuable and produces a clear demonstration-budget trade-off. Cloneability has close links to policy complexity and distillation literature, so the paper needs a predictive metric that generalizes across tasks rather than correlations within one simulator.
compute_data_notes: Public Playground-style simulators and simple BC students make data generation cheap. Multiple teachers and demonstration budgets are readily feasible on a 3080.

title: Emergent bisimulation.
rationale: Strong representation-learning fit and measurable ground truth in small domains, but heavily adjacent to bisimulation literature and feature-distance choices can make conclusions fragile.
compute_data_notes: Gridworlds, Procgen, and DMC are public; exact metrics are easy only in small domains, while Procgen seeds make the study moderately expensive.

title: How reversible is RLVR?
rationale: The reversion curve offers an interesting operational decomposition of formatting versus capability and could reveal transferable residual structure. The interpretation is not uniquely identified by reversibility, layerwise weight differences are weak mechanistic evidence, and many training combinations are required.
compute_data_notes: Procedural public data and 0.5B models are workable, but three domains, RLVR, repeated SFT reversion, transfer, and layer analysis are compute-heavy for a 3080. Tight scope is needed.

title: Agents learn clocks, and clocks break horizon generalization.
rationale: A crisp representation hypothesis, strong visualizable diagnostics, and cheap causal interventions. The principal risk is that implicit time representations and randomized horizons have close prior work, so literature differentiation is essential.
compute_data_notes: Procedural recurrent-control and gridworld tasks are public and tiny. Probes, randomized episode lengths, and adversarial penalties allow many seeds and horizon tests within a week.

title: Scoring rules for numeric answers.
rationale: The decision-theoretic prediction is rigorous and could correct common reward-shaping intuitions. Proper scoring requires eliciting distributions rather than ordinary point answers, making comparison less direct, and much of the mean/median result is established theory; empirical surprises must carry the paper.
compute_data_notes: Synthetic estimation tasks and small public models require no proprietary data. Short answers make several reward-shape runs practical on a 3080 in about a week.

title: The perfect-model gap.
rationale: A valuable oracle decomposition for model-based RL with controlled noise experiments; the true simulator changes planning cost and interfaces, and a finding that models are not limiting could be benchmark-specific.
compute_data_notes: DMC/Playground are public, but implementing simulator-backed TD-MPC2 and Dreamer planning is substantial; 10 GB and repeated imagination make two weeks optimistic but possible with small variants.

title: RL mostly teaches when to stop.
rationale: A sharp mechanistic ablation addressing a timely RLVR question, with an easily understood outcome. Termination-only parameterization is not trivial because EOS probability depends on hidden states altered by content, and related token-entropy work raises novelty risk.
compute_data_notes: GSM8K and procedural generators are public. A 0.5B LoRA model can fit in 10 GB with quantization and checkpointing, but online multi-sample generation is slow; a narrow one- to two-domain study is realistic.

title: Does TD learning sit at an edge of stability?
rationale: A crisp, mechanistic hypothesis with falsifiable scaling predictions and strong optimization relevance. It could be a strong ICML/NeurIPS paper, but recent sharpness-in-RL work creates novelty risk and the update-map Jacobian definition must be theoretically precise.
compute_data_notes: MinAtar and DMC are public and small networks make JVP power iteration practical on a 3080. Broad sweeps and enough seeds are feasible in roughly two weeks, though SAC Jacobian instrumentation may be fiddly.

title: Revealed time preference: what discount does a trained agent actually use?
rationale: A distinctive behavioral measurement with a memorable cross-disciplinary framing, clean competing functional forms, and informative negative results. Venue strength depends on proving the gadgets measure preference rather than value approximation artifacts and on broad algorithmic replication.
compute_data_notes: Gridworlds and small DMC gadgets use public simulators and little compute. Large seed counts and gamma/n-step sweeps are realistic on a single 3080 in about a week.

title: The junk tolerance curve.
rationale: A controlled dilution curve addresses a basic assumption behind shared replay and heterogeneous data, with useful capacity and similarity predictions. The flat-then-cliff hypothesis may be architecture-specific, and without a mitigation method the work could be judged descriptive.
compute_data_notes: Junk and task data can be generated from public DMC/Playground environments. Buffer mixtures and width sweeps are cheap enough for a comprehensive one-GPU study.

title: Shield reliance.
rationale: Clear safety failure mode, longitudinal metric, and simple mitigation with strong applied relevance; shield dropout resembles established robustness/domain-randomization techniques, limiting algorithmic novelty.
compute_data_notes: Safety Gymnasium and suitable Playground constraints are public; standard small control agents make a one-week 3080 study realistic.

title: Seeds versus evaluation episodes.
rationale: Statistically rigorous, directly actionable, and likely to expose common false-positive inflation; the variance-allocation result is classical statistics, so contribution depends on broad empirical evidence and usable guidance.
compute_data_notes: Gymnax/Craftax are very cheap and DMC is public; 50-by-100 evaluation is manageable, while training 50 seeds is the main one-week cost.

title: Why does scaling the actor hurt?
rationale: The question is crisp, documented, and cheap to test. It becomes genuinely strong only if the study distinguishes exploration collapse from critic exploitation causally rather than reporting correlated diagnostics.
compute_data_notes: DMC is public and the actor-only sweep is modest. True-return evaluation for selected actions needs careful counterfactual rollout design but is practical on one GPU.

title: PEGASUS at scale: common random numbers in GPU simulators.
rationale: Revisiting a principled variance-reduction idea under modern GPU simulation is timely, rigorous, and potentially impactful if it changes method rankings. Historical prior art caps novelty, and common random numbers can bias optimization toward fixed randomness unless fresh paired seeds are handled carefully.
compute_data_notes: Gymnax and GPU simulators expose public RNG control; paired tests are cheap, while competitive CRN gradient and finite-difference implementations should fit in one to two weeks.

title: Description length of the value function predicts sample complexity.
rationale: A broad, theory-adjacent hypothesis with cheap exhaustive tests and a strong negative result if MDL adds no predictive power. The fixed coder can make the conclusion arbitrary, and moving from tabular families to deep RL relevance is nontrivial.
compute_data_notes: Generated tabular and gridworld tasks need no external data and are extremely cheap. Fifty-plus tasks, exact optimal values, many seeds, and regression controls are all comfortable on one 3080 or CPU.

title: Weight decay is implicit pessimism.
rationale: Crisp sign-flip prediction, grounded mechanism, and strong ablations make this unusually falsifiable; significance depends on showing effects beyond a narrow optimizer artifact and surviving prior-art search.
compute_data_notes: SAC/IQL with DMC and D4RL is comfortably 3080-scale; all environments and offline datasets are public, and one week is plausible.

title: A bandwidth law for coordination.
rationale: A predictive information-performance law would be broadly significant, quantitative, and more durable than another communication architecture. Estimating the relevant mutual information and defining oracle optimal actions in complex MARL tasks are the hard parts.
compute_data_notes: JaxMARL tasks are public and small, but capacity sweeps across several games and stable multi-agent seeds create a substantial two-week workload.

title: The effective horizon of a trained critic.
rationale: A concrete influence-based quantity with direct connection to credit-assignment failure and useful ablations; editable-reward interventions must be defined carefully to avoid off-distribution artifacts.
compute_data_notes: Small public cloneable simulators are enough; checkpoint probes add moderate cost but fit easily on one 3080 in about a week.

title: What fraction of actor updates are actually improvements?
rationale: A memorable and broadly informative measurement enabled by common random numbers, with clear algorithm comparisons; it needs rigorous confidence intervals and must show predictive value beyond being descriptive.
compute_data_notes: Brax/Mujoco Playground are public, but evaluating nearly every update adds substantial simulator work; GPU parallelism keeps it feasible on one 3080.

title: A learned curriculum over relabeling horizon.
rationale: Turning an informational diagnosis into an adaptive method is crisp and testable. Online mutual-information estimation can be noisy and expensive, so the paper needs a convincing estimator and matched-compute controls.
compute_data_notes: HER/CRL environments and manipulation suites are public. Small policies fit easily; MI estimator tuning and horizon-schedule baselines are the main burdens.

title: An audit of world-model hallucination.
rationale: A systematic reachability metric tied to policy exploitation could be significant. The hard part is defining unreachable latent states without a circular learned classifier; DMC ground-truth state makes a credible restricted study possible.
compute_data_notes: DMC supplies simulator state and is public. Reachability labels may require resettable simulator rollouts or carefully generated negatives, while Dreamer training itself remains manageable at small scale.

title: The basin of attraction shrinks late in training.
rationale: The hypothesized non-monotonic trajectory is surprising, measurable, and important for robustness reporting. Basin volume depends strongly on chosen initial-state measure and goal threshold, so broad significance requires principled definitions and causal tests of entropy/overconfidence.
compute_data_notes: Checkpoint evaluation from wide initial states is embarrassingly parallel in public GPU simulators. It adds modest cost and is very feasible on one 3080.

title: Sign accuracy of policy-gradient estimators.
rationale: A direction-quality metric against high-sample gradients is methodologically strong, falsifiable, and may explain why variance fails to predict learning. Coordinatewise sign depends on parameterization, so invariant alternatives and confidence intervals for ground truth are crucial.
compute_data_notes: GPU-native public simulators make high-sample gradients plausible; 100k-sample references at many checkpoints are costly but manageable on focused small tasks.

title: Safety is forgotten first.
rationale: Important fine-tuning question with a testable ordering and preservation intervention; attribution-defined low-rank subspaces are underspecified and may weaken causal claims.
compute_data_notes: Public constrained-control tasks suffice, but shifts, attribution, and low-rank freezing require multiple stages and seeds; feasible in roughly two weeks on one GPU.

title: Depth, normalization, and plasticity in one controlled sweep.
rationale: The three-way interaction is timely and visually clear, with good ICLR fit. As written it is a large factorial ablation; it needs a mechanistic prediction and controls for parameter count and optimization to rise above synthesis.
compute_data_notes: Craftax is cheap, but continual DMC plus depth to 128, normalization conditions, task sequences, and seeds is a large matrix. A focused benchmark subset is credible on one 3080.

title: Zero-shot coordination via shared world models.
rationale: Zero-shot cross-play is a strong metric and world models offer a plausible new approach. The phrase 'includes the partner' leaves the actual method vague, and robust held-out partner populations are costly to create.
compute_data_notes: Overcooked-JAX is public and fast, but training diverse partner populations plus world-model and model-free agents across layouts and seeds is substantial on one GPU.

title: Exact double sampling via cloning.
rationale: This cleanly resolves a classic estimator obstacle and enables a decisive modern reassessment of residual gradients. It has strong methodological fit, though impact falls sharply if exact gradients still lose and simulator cloning limits applicability.
compute_data_notes: Requires a public simulator with reliable state clone/restore and independent transition noise; the core runs are moderate, but implementing exact paired successors correctly is nontrivial.

title: Exposure bias in multi-turn RL.
rationale: A sensible transfer of a classic issue with an excellent planted-error recovery test, but scheduled sampling is established and language-agent training choices may reduce perceived novelty.
compute_data_notes: TextWorld and BabyAI are public; 0.5–1B rollout-heavy training fits with LoRA on 10 GB but two weeks is a realistic minimum.

title: Pathwise gradients through a world model vs. through Q.
rationale: The bias comparison is fundamental and measurable, with strong ICML fit. A fair controlled implementation is difficult because Dreamer and Q-gradient agents differ in representation, replay, and objectives beyond the gradient path.
compute_data_notes: DMC provides public simulator dynamics and counterfactual evaluation. Building truly matched agents and estimating gradient bias is engineering-heavy but possible with a narrowed task set.

title: The RLVR size floor.
rationale: A meaningful scaling/mechanism study with a clear pass@k predictor, but adjacent scaling work is likely and proving a compute-independent floor is stronger than finite experiments can support.
compute_data_notes: Pythia/SmolLM weights and procedural tasks are public; 1.5B LoRA fits tightly on 10 GB, while pass@1024 and many sizes make a thorough two-week sweep difficult.

title: Memory in the world model vs. memory in the policy.
rationale: The prediction-versus-control factorization is conceptually clean and may reveal a useful structural principle. Toy POMDP-only evidence could limit significance, so one richer environment and strict capacity matching would help.
compute_data_notes: Custom POMDPs are cheap and need no dataset. Small RSSM and recurrent-policy agents fit easily, permitting extensive seeds and horizon sweeps.

title: Lazy critics: how much of Q depends on the action?
rationale: The action-sensitivity onset is an intuitive, measurable mechanism connecting critic learning to actor failure, with a direct intervention. It needs normalization controls because state and action gradient norms are parameterization-sensitive.
compute_data_notes: DMC and standard MuJoCo data generation are public and cheap. MyoSuite and Playground broaden the claim but may require installation work; gradient logging and the auxiliary loss are inexpensive on a 3080.

title: Predicting plasticity collapse before it happens.
rationale: Forecasting plus gated intervention is a crisp diagnostic-to-method pipeline. The central risk is leakage and weak out-of-distribution forecasting across seeds, tasks, or algorithms; per-run fitted forecasters would be unconvincing.
compute_data_notes: Small continual-RL environments are public and spectral logging is affordable. Training labels require enough collapse events, but runs can be generated on one GPU in a reasonable timeframe.

title: First-success lock-in.
rationale: A sharp causal intervention on path dependence with memorable behavioral outcomes; first-trajectory replacement can create distribution artifacts and multi-solution mode metrics need careful definition.
compute_data_notes: Public Craftax/Procgen plus synthetic gridworlds are modest; branching many seeds after first success is practical on one 3080.

title: Vine at scale: zero-variance counterfactual advantages.
rationale: Reviving vine estimation under a materially changed compute primitive is timely and has a clean variance-versus-cost evaluation. The claim of zero variance is overstated under stochastic futures, and cloning overhead plus old prior art reduce novelty.
compute_data_notes: Brax-style public simulators are cloneable, but exact state branching infrastructure is nontrivial and N branches multiply rollout cost. Small continuous-control tasks fit on a 3080; broad compute-matched evidence may take two weeks.

title: Restating the problem as an action.
rationale: Creative, testable, and strengthened by cross-model transfer of restatements; it may be judged close to learned prompting or latent scratchpad work unless the canonicalization mechanism is analyzed convincingly.
compute_data_notes: Procedural word/graph data are cheap and public; two sub-billion models with LoRA fit a 3080, with rollout generation taking roughly two weeks.

title: The information content of feedback in code RL.
rationale: A model-size-by-feedback-information threshold is a clear empirical question with practical agent implications. Without an information-theoretic treatment it may look like a scaling ablation, and 0.5B-1.5B models may be too weak for meaningful multi-turn code correction.
compute_data_notes: Procedural coding tasks and open models are available, but four feedback conditions, three sizes, RL training, and execution rollouts are expensive. Restricting sizes/tasks makes it possible on a 3080 in two to three weeks.

title: Temperature as an action.
rationale: Per-problem adaptive sampling is useful and the learned token offers an interpretable difficulty signal. Temperature is normally an external sampling parameter, so differentiating or assigning credit through it is technically nontrivial; simpler confidence-conditioned or entropy-control baselines may subsume the idea.
compute_data_notes: Open 0.5B-1B models and procedural benchmarks suffice. Sampling multiple temperatures raises rollout cost modestly but remains feasible on a single 3080.

title: Value Gradient Flow for discrete actions.
rationale: A successful discrete formulation would be a real methodological extension, but Gumbel and straight-through bias are obvious baselines rather than clear novelty. Atari results need enough games to demonstrate more than a toy proof.
compute_data_notes: MinAtar is cheap and public; Atari-100k is much heavier. Discrete relaxation tuning and test-time scaling multiply experiments, though a focused subset remains possible.

title: Shaping ruggedness: how many local optima does a dense reward create?
rationale: An appealing reward-design diagnostic with held-out validation, but endpoint cluster count is representation- and threshold-sensitive and may not correspond to true policy-space local optima.
compute_data_notes: Public Playground tasks and many short GPU-parallel runs make 100+ seeds realistic; clustering and shaping variants require no external data.

title: How much memory does a task need?
rationale: A task-level memory statistic that predicts architecture choice would be broadly useful and has a clean cross-suite test. Predicting optimal action from windows depends on policy quality and data coverage, so the estimator may measure dataset ambiguity rather than intrinsic memory.
compute_data_notes: POPGym and MemoryGym are public and small; Atari broadening is costly, but a focused suite plus DMC perturbations is feasible in one to two weeks.

title: Quasimetric value heads in world models.
rationale: This combines two current ideas around a specific generalization hypothesis and has a clean near-to-far test. Risk comes from architectural ambiguity and the possibility that gains follow from generic metric regularization.
compute_data_notes: Goal-conditioned mazes and modest manipulation tasks are public or easy to generate. A small Dreamer configuration and focused two-domain evaluation fit one GPU.

title: When do decoder-free world models fail?
rationale: A controlled boundary map plus selector is a solid representation-learning paper. The selector based on reconstruction-error variance is underspecified for a decoder-free model, and building fair perceptual dials across environments is nontrivial.
compute_data_notes: DMC and Procgen are public, but three world-model systems across a factorial visual suite and seeds are demanding on a 10 GB GPU. Narrowing to one controlled suite is advisable.

title: The actor's state distribution is a free hyperparameter.
rationale: Extremely simple, useful, and cleanly testable, with potentially broad practical impact; novelty may be challenged by replay recency and emphatic/off-policy policy-gradient literature.
compute_data_notes: A one-line sampling change on public DMC/Playground; low memory, no special data, and days of 3080 compute are credible.

title: Two-speed critics: fast heads, slow trunks.
rationale: Plausible layerwise mechanism and practical target-network alternative, but per-layer learning rates are established and the claim of removing target networks needs unusually broad, stable results.
compute_data_notes: Public DMC/MinAtar, small models, and ordinary sweeps are easily within a 3080-week.

title: Off-policy evaluation of exploration policies.
rationale: Extending OPE from return to coverage is methodologically interesting and could save substantial evaluation compute. The hard support problem is fundamental, and learned abstractions may make estimates appear successful only in forgiving settings.
compute_data_notes: Craftax and MinAtar are public and cheap enough to obtain ground-truth policy coverage. Density-ratio baselines are computationally light, but generating enough policies and datasets for convincing validation takes roughly two weeks.

title: Where to imagine from.
rationale: Allocating imagination by expected learning value is sensible and potentially useful, but prioritized model rollouts have close precedents and the proposed signals may favor model-error hotspots. Strong controls against prioritized replay and model uncertainty are necessary.
compute_data_notes: Dreamer small can run on DMC, but Atari-100k, checkpoint return estimates, and prioritization sweeps strain a single 10GB GPU. Public data/environments are available; two-plus weeks is realistic for restricted scope.

title: Planted-error recovery as a transfer metric.
rationale: Controlled error injection is an excellent evaluation protocol that separates recovery from first-pass competence and enables cross-domain claims. The main risk is contamination by unnatural prefixes and difficulty making planted errors comparable across domains.
compute_data_notes: Public procedural generation is available; evaluation is cheap once models exist, but training multiple RLVR models at 0.5–1.5B remains demanding on 10 GB.

title: What does "sample efficiency" mean when env steps are free?
rationale: The GPU-native environment shift makes this a timely and practical evaluation question. It needs more than a wall-clock leaderboard: a decomposition of environment, update, and scaling costs should yield transferable conclusions.
compute_data_notes: Mujoco Playground is public and specifically optimized for a single GPU. Four algorithms and matched wall-clock runs are feasible, though framework-level optimization fairness is critical.

title: A learned prompt-level baseline replaces the group.
rationale: A practical and well-scoped variance-cost trade-off that could materially reduce GRPO rollout expense. Learned contextual baselines and reward models are conceptually close, so novelty depends on rigorous matched-budget results and a predictive crossover analysis.
compute_data_notes: Public procedural and math prompts suffice. A scalar prompt head is cheap, but the group-size grid requires many online generations; 0.5B quantized LoRA is feasible on 10 GB with limited tasks and seeds.

title: Which part of a world-model agent loses plasticity first?
rationale: Component-level diagnosis is novel and has a clear intervention test, with especially good representation-learning fit. However, defining comparable plasticity metrics across heterogeneous Dreamer components is difficult and could yield descriptive results.
compute_data_notes: DreamerV3 code and DMC/Craftax are public, but component diagnostics, task switching, resets/clipping, and enough seeds create a heavy experiment matrix for a 3080.

title: Advantage sign agreement across checkpoints as free uncertainty.
rationale: A cheap temporal uncertainty signal with a direct error-correlation test and ensemble comparison is attractive. However, snapshot disagreement is not truly free in storage/evaluation and may mainly track nonstationarity, so it needs calibration and strong uncertainty baselines.
compute_data_notes: Recent snapshots and Monte Carlo validation are inexpensive for DMC actors and critics. Public code and data generation make completion on one 3080 straightforward.

title: Random networks as macro-actions.
rationale: Simple, creative exploration prior with decisive baselines and sparse-task metrics; it risks being seen as another correlated-noise variant unless coherent behaviors and consistent gains are demonstrated.
compute_data_notes: Public sparse DMC, Craftax, and MinAtar fit easily; many exploration seeds are affordable on a single 3080 in a week.

title: The reset subsidy.
rationale: A clean benchmark quantity that improves reset-free comparisons and links to state-distribution drift; continuing-task definitions and return comparability under different reset rates need careful normalization.
compute_data_notes: DMC/Playground are public and reset schedules are simple; long no-reset trajectories add modest cost and are feasible in a week on one 3080.

title: How often does a policy need to look?
rationale: A useful deployment quantity with a dynamics-based prediction and clean train-test matrices; observation staleness and control frequency are well-studied, so novelty rests on the Lyapunov-rate relationship.
compute_data_notes: Public DMC/Playground and small policies fit well; the staleness matrix is broad but easily parallelized on a 3080.

title: Do exploration bonuses create habits?
rationale: A useful and clean post-annealing measurement with an actionable actor-only intervention; residual behavior may be expected policy inertia, so a deeper mechanism is needed for top-tier novelty.
compute_data_notes: MinAtar/Craftax and standard RND/count methods are public and small; checkpoint branching fits comfortably into a one-week 3080 budget.

title: Start-state generalization in offline RL.
rationale: Exposes an under-tested offline-RL failure and may reverse rankings, but reachable out-of-coverage starts can be arbitrary and the specific prediction about IQL is uncertain; protocol design is the contribution.
compute_data_notes: D4RL and OGBench are public and offline training is 3080-friendly; simulator state-reset support and five-method replication push the study toward two weeks.

title: A cognitive-bias battery for control agents.
rationale: A standardized battery with mechanism ablations is distinctive and could become useful infrastructure, especially for AAAI. Human-bias labels risk anthropomorphism, and the proposed one-mechanism-per-bias attributions are likely too neat; predictive deployment validity is needed.
compute_data_notes: Gridworld and small continuous gadgets are public or easy to implement. Four algorithms, variants, and many seeds remain cheap on a 3080.

title: Null-space exploration.
rationale: A concrete directional exploration method with a high-dimensional control motivation, but a single scalar Q gradient has a large trivial orthogonal space and low gradient need not mean uncertainty.
compute_data_notes: MyoSuite is public; Shadow Hand can be costly and 10 GB constrains parallelism, but a focused suite and automatic differentiation are feasible in about two weeks.

title: Does RLVR on procedural tasks transfer to natural-language phrasings of the same tasks?
rationale: The format-versus-reasoning question is important and paired inputs give a clean evaluation. It is more diagnostic than methodological, and verbalization quality or pretraining contamination can confound conclusions.
compute_data_notes: Paired symbolic/verbal data can be generated publicly and cheaply. LoRA RLVR for three domains at 0.5B is workable, while 1.5B on 10 GB would require aggressive quantization and slow training.

title: The world model is only good where the policy went.
rationale: Policy-conditioned model error is central to model-based RL and diversified collection gives a direct intervention. The premise is partly established as distribution shift/model exploitation, so novelty rests on a compelling measurement and gains over uncertainty-aware exploration.
compute_data_notes: DMC is public, but reliable DreamerV3-small and TD-MPC2 baselines, held-out-policy evaluation, and seeds are demanding for a 10 GB 3080; scope likely must be reduced.

title: Compute-optimal actor-critic: parameters vs. update-to-data ratio vs. env steps at fixed GPU-hours.
rationale: Compute allocation is important, but a Chinchilla-style law needs much broader scale and budgets than nine tasks to be credible. A local frontier is publishable only if the accounting and held-out predictions are unusually clean.
compute_data_notes: Public simulators suffice, but a dense three-dimensional grid with seeds and held-out validation is expensive on one 3080. Wall-clock measurements are also hardware- and implementation-specific.

title: Adam's ε is a hidden learning-rate schedule in TD learning.
rationale: A clean, overlooked optimizer diagnostic with useful reward-scale implications, but likely viewed as an empirical implementation finding unless backed by theory and broad causal evidence.
compute_data_notes: Very cheap small-network SAC/DQN/PPO runs on public DMC and MinAtar; logging optimizer statistics needs negligible extra memory.

title: Time-limit truncation is right-censoring. Use survival analysis.
rationale: The statistical reframing is elegant and falsifiable, with a natural theoretical component. However, censoring assumptions may fail under policy-dependent trajectories and beating correct bootstrapping is a demanding baseline.
compute_data_notes: Standard public control tasks can be modified with short limits. Tobit or survival objectives are cheap; synthetic environments with known uncensored values can establish correctness without heavy compute.

title: Budget-aware exploration.
rationale: Conditioning behavior on remaining training budget is practically relevant and yields interpretable schedules, but the state variable is artificial and comparisons to per-budget tuned schedules are demanding. The novelty may be viewed as schedule meta-learning unless cross-budget generalization is compelling.
compute_data_notes: MinAtar, Craftax, and sparse control benchmarks are public. Three budgets times baselines and seeds are manageable, though the 8M-step condition can stretch a one-GPU timeline.

title: Actor–critic feature misalignment predicts instability.
rationale: Interesting representation-level coupling with a testable precursor and intervention, but gradient attributions are noisy and 'cannot follow' is not logically implied by input-feature disagreement.
compute_data_notes: Public DMC/MyoSuite fit; attribution computation across training adds overhead but remains practical in a week on one 3080.

title: A taxonomy of nonstationarity and which plasticity fix works for which.
rationale: Controlled nonstationarity types and a method-by-type result are useful and falsifiable, with good AAAI breadth. Venue competitiveness falls if it remains a lookup table without principles predicting method effectiveness.
compute_data_notes: A custom gridworld or Craftax family avoids proprietary data and is cheap. Implementing five fixes consistently is the main engineering and fairness burden.

title: Compute-optimal allocation between verifier samples and policy samples.
rationale: A useful resource-allocation question with scope for a statistical crossover law. Controllable synthetic verifier noise may not represent structured judge errors, and a compelling paper needs theory plus validation with real noisy verifiers.
compute_data_notes: Procedural tasks and test-case subsampling provide public controllable settings. Small-model LoRA is possible on 10 GB, but the two-dimensional allocation grid multiplies costly rollout training.

title: Reward-epistemic exploration.
rationale: The distinction between confirmed-empty and merely unvisited regions is clear and experimentally controllable. Reward-model uncertainty bonuses are conceptually close to existing exploration and model-uncertainty work, so competitiveness requires a strong regime map rather than modest RND gains.
compute_data_notes: Synthetic mazes, MinAtar, and Craftax are public and small reward ensembles are cheap. The proposed reward-free-fraction sweep is highly feasible on one 3080.

title: Hack discovery time vs compute.
rationale: Controlled scaling laws for reward hacking address an important claim and can produce useful null results. Capacity, UTD, and exploration are not one compute axis, while exploit distance needs an operational definition that does not predetermine the exponent.
compute_data_notes: Injected exploits can be built in public lightweight environments; many seeds over several capacity axes are compute-heavy but possible in roughly two weeks.

title: Automatic update-to-data ratio from a spectral signal.
rationale: Removing UTD tuning is practical and the matched-compute evaluation is well specified. The novelty hinges on a stable causal relation between the spectral signal and overfitting rather than a controller with newly tuned thresholds.
compute_data_notes: DMC is public and feasible. Online eNTK estimation can be costly, and fixed UTD baselines across several values multiply runs; cheaper approximations may be necessary.

title: Adaptive imagination horizon.
rationale: A natural uncertainty-aware extension with clear baselines, but adaptive rollout truncation and disagreement ensembles are established motifs. Novelty and gains must exceed the extra ensemble compute and calibration burden.
compute_data_notes: DMC is practical; Atari plus an ensemble is much heavier and may exceed 10 GB without sequential models or tiny configurations. Public environments and implementations exist.

title: Dense-to-sparse reward curricula for sub-1B RLVR.
rationale: The schedule is clear and useful, but reward curricula are crowded and one QA setting would look incremental. Strong results need insight into when switching works and transfer beyond the anchor setup.
compute_data_notes: MuSiQue is public, but GRPO with three schedules, three seeds, and 0.8B models on a 10 GB 3080 is tight. Quantization, LoRA, short contexts, and small groups are required.

title: Spectral health as a universal early-stopping signal for RL.
rationale: One signal across algorithms and three decisions would be significant if it generalizes, but the scope is too broad and 'spectral health' is underspecified. Early stopping, resets, and UTD control have different targets and likely need distinct calibration.
compute_data_notes: Piggybacking only helps if relevant runs already exist; from scratch, SAC, PPO, and Dreamer across DMC and Atari with spectral logging is expensive. eNTK measurement further increases cost.

title: Intra-trajectory negatives: why do they stabilize contrastive RL?
rationale: Mechanistically separating hardness, horizon, and false negatives is a good falsifiable study. It needs carefully constructed interventions because these factors are naturally coupled; otherwise it remains an ablation note.
compute_data_notes: BuilderBench-GPU and point-maze are cheap, assuming stable public implementations. Negative samplers and enough seeds are straightforward on one GPU.

title: Anti-goals.
rationale: Negative conditioning is an intuitive safety interface with clear held-out hazard tests and good application fit. The novelty claim needs careful literature review around constrained, avoidance-conditioned, and multi-goal RL, and hazard-type generalization may require richer representations.
compute_data_notes: Maze tasks are cheap and public; manipulation hazards add meaningful evidence but setup and seeds push the project toward two weeks.

title: Classical control margins for RL policies.
rationale: Bridging classical margins and empirical deep-RL robustness has broad significance and a clear predictive evaluation. Applying local linear metrics to nonlinear, nonstationary trajectories is technically delicate, and existing robust-control literature must be distinguished carefully.
compute_data_notes: Public control suites provide all data; simulator Jacobians or finite differences across many trajectory points add engineering and evaluation cost but not prohibitive GPU demand.

title: Value discontinuities at contact.
rationale: Contact geometry supplies a strong mechanism and a contact-gated critic is a concrete architectural response. True discounted Q may be less discontinuous than instantaneous dynamics, and proving improvement on fine manipulation with small-scale training is difficult.
compute_data_notes: MyoSuite and Playground are public, but contact-rich manipulation is seed-sensitive and slower; two weeks on a 3080 is plausible only with a focused task set.

title: Where in depth is the answer decided, before and after RL?
rationale: Good ICLR mechanistic fit and clear before/after analyses, but logit-lens and attention interpretations are contested, correlational, and likely crowded in current RLVR work.
compute_data_notes: Public 0.5–1.5B models and synthetic tasks suffice; activation storage and 1.5B inference strain 10 GB but quantization or smaller models keep it feasible.

title: Notes across episodes.
rationale: Learning a transferable natural-language memory artifact from return alone is distinctive and empirically legible. Credit assignment across episodes, text-game interaction cost, and avoiding notes that merely encode instance IDs make successful execution risky on small hardware.
compute_data_notes: TextWorld/BabyAI-style environments are public, but long-horizon RL over 0.5–1B generation plus cross-model transfer is likely beyond a comfortable two-week 3080 budget without heavy simplification.

title: Anticipatory targets: compute TD targets with the actor you will have, not the one you have.
rationale: The method is simple, testable, and tied to a clear lag mechanism, but it risks reading as a narrow SAC/TD3 trick unless accompanied by analysis showing when extrapolation should help and robust gains over tuned baselines.
compute_data_notes: Public DMC tasks and modest actor-critic networks fit easily. A focused kappa, learning-rate, and UTD sweep is highly feasible on one 3080 within one to two weeks.

title: Within-task forgetting: the agent forgets its stepping stones.
rationale: A compelling reframing of replay failure with an interpretable intervention. Attribution is difficult because TD error on old transitions can legitimately change, and Montezuma-scale evidence may be too expensive.
compute_data_notes: Craftax and maze benchmarks are public; use MiniHack or a lightweight Montezuma-style task rather than full Atari. Tagging and anchor replay are cheap, making a focused study feasible on one GPU.

title: Inaction baselines for multi-agent credit.
rationale: Interpretable and economical counterfactual credit with useful free-rider analysis, but no-op semantics are environment-dependent and COMA-style counterfactual baselines make novelty vulnerable.
compute_data_notes: JaxMARL environments are public; exact cloning/branching and hand-labeled contribution data add engineering, but small agents fit a 3080 within two weeks.

title: Domain randomization inside imagination.
rationale: The method is simple and robustness evaluation is clean, but latent noise or dropout as domain randomization may look like standard regularization. It needs evidence that perturbations correspond to meaningful dynamics uncertainty.
compute_data_notes: DMC mass and friction shifts are public and inexpensive. Dreamer plus several perturbation strengths and explicit simulator-domain-randomization baselines is feasible on one GPU.

title: Data attribution for RL.
rationale: Behavior-level attribution in a moving-target, self-generated setting is important and exploit removal gives a causal validation. TracIn approximations may be unreliable for replay and bootstrapping, and recent related work creates material novelty risk.
compute_data_notes: Injected-exploit MinAtar/Procgen data can be generated publicly; checkpoint-gradient storage and per-transition influence calculations are memory- and engineering-heavy but manageable on small networks.

title: Which part of a critic is about the policy, and which about the world?
rationale: A potentially interesting representation result with transfer implications, especially for ICLR. The policy-invariant subspace is underspecified and CCA similarity may not establish semantic invariance or yield a learnable decomposition.
compute_data_notes: Public small control environments suffice, but training critics for 50 diverse policies plus representation analyses creates substantial run count. Small networks and one environment keep it practical in two to three weeks.

title: Where does seed variance come from? A factorial decomposition.
rationale: Broadly useful methodological evidence with a rigorous factorial design and informative null results. The contribution is measurement rather than algorithmic novelty, so venue strength depends on surprising, actionable findings across multiple algorithm classes.
compute_data_notes: Gymnax and Craftax are public and tiny. Controlled seeds and deterministic settings require engineering care, but many runs can be completed quickly on one 3080.

title: Disagreement across discount factors as an exploration signal.
rationale: A simple, falsifiable exploration signal with inexpensive baselines and a meaningful redundancy test. Its conceptual weakness is that different discounts encode different objectives, not epistemic uncertainty, so disagreement may systematically reward delay rather than information.
compute_data_notes: MinAtar, Craftax, and sparse DMC are public. Multi-head critics add little memory or runtime, enabling broad baselines and seeds on a single 3080.

title: The critical batch size of TD learning changes over training.
rationale: Useful optimization study with a concrete schedule and unique-versus-duplicate ablation, though critical-batch-size transfer from supervised learning is somewhat incremental and moving TD targets complicate interpretation.
compute_data_notes: Public DMC/MinAtar and small agents fit easily; many batch-size sweeps are run-heavy but practical within a week using efficient implementations.

title: Inverse-task RL as an auxiliary.
rationale: The matched-compute forward-versus-inverse test is clean and representation-oriented, and benefits across several task families would be notable. Problem generation and cycle consistency have extensive prior art, so the RL auxiliary must show more than synthetic-data augmentation.
compute_data_notes: Arithmetic, graph, and logic data can be procedural, but multi-domain RL fine-tuning and verification at 0.5–1B is tight on one 3080.

title: Asymmetric capacity in cooperative teams.
rationale: Matched-total-capacity allocation is an underexplored MARL design axis and yields an interpretable symmetry/planning prediction. The leader-follower explanation is correlational, and heterogeneous observations or roles can confound results; methodological novelty is moderate.
compute_data_notes: JaxMARL environments and small networks are public and efficient. Capacity splits, seeds, and causal analyses are feasible on one 3080 in one to two weeks.

title: Decide only when it matters.
rationale: Using action sensitivity for adaptive temporal abstraction is simple and interpretable, with plausible control benefits. Raw critic gradients are noisy and scale-dependent, and learned action-repeat/event-triggered control is crowded, making baseline quality and normalization decisive.
compute_data_notes: DMC and related public simulators fit comfortably, but MyoSuite breadth increases wall-clock time. Gradient computation and fixed-repeat baselines are practical on a 3080.

title: The fresh-critic gap as a reset trigger.
rationale: The refit oracle is an intuitive diagnostic and produces a concrete adaptive reset method. Novelty is vulnerable to recent reset, primacy-bias, and critic-reinitialization literature, while repeated refits need strict matched-compute accounting.
compute_data_notes: SAC/DQN and their public benchmarks are light, though periodic multi-seed refits multiply training cost. A focused experiment is feasible in two weeks on one GPU.

title: Plasticity under opponent nonstationarity.
rationale: The cross-literature connection is interesting and AAAI-friendly, but self-play plateaus have many causes and spectral correlations will not establish plasticity as the cause. Strong controls against cycling and game-theoretic non-convergence are essential.
compute_data_notes: MPE and Overcooked-JAX are public and modest. Self-play evaluation needs populations, checkpoints, cross-play, and seeds, increasing compute and experimental complexity.

title: Does RLVR make models stubborn or sycophantic?
rationale: Assertion robustness is cheap and societally relevant, with a straightforward training intervention. The metric is narrow, closely adjacent to existing sycophancy work, and could conflate greater confidence with better reasoning unless assertions include calibrated correct and incorrect controls.
compute_data_notes: Public small models and synthetic prompts are sufficient. Short-context RLVR plus evaluations are feasible on a 3080 within a week or two.

title: A predictor for how big the critic should be.
rationale: A useful predictive rule could be strong, but task statistics from random rollouts may be weak proxies and 15–20 tasks may not support a robust scaling claim. It risks becoming an empirical regression with limited mechanism.
compute_data_notes: DMC and MyoSuite are public and small networks fit easily. The width-by-task-by-seed matrix is substantial but manageable with careful task selection and parallel environment execution.

title: Stigmergy: communication only through the environment.
rationale: A compelling multi-agent application with interpretable emergent conventions and a strong cross-play test. Learned stigmergy has likely adjacent prior art, and custom environment design can make success overly dependent on inductive bias.
compute_data_notes: A custom JAX gridworld needs no proprietary data and is computationally tiny. Many populations, partners, and ablations fit easily on one GPU; environment and protocol design dominate effort.

title: The Bellman wavefront.
rationale: The wavefront is an interpretable new measurement with strong visual and predictive potential, and it connects diagnostics to n-step or reset interventions. Generalizing distance and ground-truth value beyond small environments is the central limitation.
compute_data_notes: Gridworld studies are trivial; low-dimensional control requires discretization or dense state sampling but remains feasible with public simulators in one to two weeks.

title: The curse of context: extra history hurts on Markov tasks.
rationale: Timely representation question with a data-scaling prediction and mitigation, but context-length effects on Markov control are likely studied and transformer/MLP capacity confounds are substantial.
compute_data_notes: Public DMC/Playground and modest sequence models fit a 3080; the context-by-data matrix is broad but practical in about a week.

title: Fine-tuning when the dynamics changed, not just the distribution.
rationale: Dynamics shift is realistic and under-benchmarked, with strong applied-AI relevance. As written it is an evaluation paper rather than a new method; competitiveness rises if it reveals a distinct mechanism or motivates a successful adaptation.
