compute_data_notes: MuJoCo physics perturbations and offline datasets are public, cheap, and easy to control. Three methods across several shifts and seeds fit one 3080.

title: How often is the optimal action set multimodal?
rationale: A timely measurement that could test a major premise behind generative policies and is particularly suitable for ICLR. Mode counting in high-dimensional action spaces is threshold-sensitive, and learned critics can manufacture modes.
compute_data_notes: DMC and MyoSuite are public. Reliable Monte Carlo landscapes and Gaussian-versus-flow comparisons are expensive, especially for high-dimensional hands, so low-dimensional scans plus targeted manipulation cases are realistic.

title: Learning when to ask for a hint.
rationale: Costed verified hints create a clean selective-prediction problem and calibration analysis, with strong application appeal. Prior help-seeking and tool-use work is crowded, and the claim that hint access improves no-hint performance needs careful leakage controls.
compute_data_notes: Procedural tasks can supply free verified hints, but RL fine-tuning several 0.5–1B models and cost sweeps is memory- and rollout-intensive on a 3080.

title: A predictability bonus for coordination.
rationale: The opposite-of-novelty bonus is memorable and could produce useful conventions without explicit symmetries. It is close to legibility, influence, and predictable-agent objectives, and may collapse to dull but mutually predictable behavior rather than robust coordination.
compute_data_notes: JaxMARL is public and cheap, and held-out-seed cross-play is straightforward. One 3080 is ample for a focused one-to-two-week study.

title: Counterfactual information gain per action.
rationale: The noisy-TV target is clear and counterfactual branching is attractive, but outcome spread is not itself information gain and can still reward irrelevant stochastic controllability. The objective needs a more rigorous definition.
compute_data_notes: Gridworld, MinAtar, and Craftax are public and cheap. State cloning is simple in custom gridworlds and manageable elsewhere; comparisons to RND and ICM fit within one to two weeks.

title: Are plateaus-then-jumps in RL grokking?
rationale: ICLR-friendly representation story and good exploration-versus-representation distinction, but the grokking analogy is easy to overclaim and the proposed signatures are correlational rather than decisive.
compute_data_notes: Craftax, MinAtar, and DMC are public and small; sufficient seeds for rare jumps are the main cost, still reasonable on a 3080.

title: Cross-action interference in discrete-action critics.
rationale: A clean representation and architecture question with a direct measurement and intervention. It risks overlap with gradient interference, action-value decomposition, and multi-head architectures, so novelty requires more than showing decoupled heads help.
compute_data_notes: Atari-100k and Procgen are public. A selected game set and lightweight architectures fit in 10 GB, although enough seeds across action counts likely takes around two weeks.

title: What do different seeds learn? Strategy modes.
rationale: A valuable methodology paper if modes are robust to representation and clustering choices and predict transfer or variance. Pure post-hoc clustering is vulnerable to subjective metrics and may not support the discrete-mode premise.
compute_data_notes: All benchmarks are public, but 30-plus seeds across three suites is run-heavy. Small Craftax, Procgen, and DMC selections plus trajectory embeddings are achievable on one GPU in two to three weeks.

title: Where does critic-ensemble diversity come from?
rationale: A factorial decomposition of ensemble disagreement could unify exploration and pessimism results and guide cheaper designs. The binary init-versus-data-order framing may omit target and bootstrap effects, and the paper needs downstream causal evidence rather than disagreement plots.
compute_data_notes: Public sparse and offline tasks suffice; independent ensembles multiply memory and compute but small networks keep a one-to-two-week study realistic.

title: Vine advantages for LLM agents in text environments.
rationale: Per-step counterfactual advantages for language agents are novel and concrete, but the comparison to sequence-level GRPO mixes credit assignment with greatly expanded branching compute. TextWorld scale may also limit broad significance.
compute_data_notes: TextWorld and BabyAI-text are public, and 0.5B LoRA can fit with quantization or checkpointing. Repeated branched generation is slow and memory tight on a 10 GB 3080, making robust multi-seed RL runs difficult.

title: Does the actor need a correct critic, or just a correctly ordered one?
rationale: The decomposition is useful and the ordering-only critic is falsifiable, but ranking critics and preference-style value learning are established enough that the paper needs a sharper theoretical explanation and broad wins to escape incremental status.
compute_data_notes: DMC is easy and public; MyoSuite is public but slower and more fragile. Monte Carlo action-order ground truth and matched-compute multi-seed runs are feasible but likely take two to three weeks.

title: Which self-verifiable pretext games are hackable?
rationale: Verifier gaming is important and the comparative framing is useful, especially for AAAI. Human-rated open-ended quality is expensive and noisy, two proposed games are underspecified, and small-model findings may not generalize.
compute_data_notes: Public summarization data exists, but credible creative-writing quality requires human annotation unavailable for free at scale. Multiple RL runs on 0.5–1B models are possible but slow.

title: Cross-simulator generalization as a cheap proxy for sim-to-real.
rationale: A validated proxy could materially improve robotics methodology, but the central claim cannot be established from published rankings alone and one real-robot test is likely underpowered. Simulator implementation differences also create severe confounds.
compute_data_notes: MuJoCo and Brax are public, while matching tasks across Isaac and obtaining comparable real-robot results is difficult. Three simulator stacks and any physical validation exceed a reasonable one-3080 project timeframe.

title: Wall-clock-matched leaderboard for sample-efficient RL.
rationale: Compute-aware ranking is timely, but wall-clock results are hardware and implementation dependent, and sharing the impossible scale of idea 46 undermines feasibility. A standardized operation-count analysis might generalize better.
compute_data_notes: Atari and implementations are public, but a statistically credible multi-agent leaderboard is far beyond a short one-3080 campaign. Strict inference and training measurement adds engineering rather than reducing runs.

title: Where should optimism live in a world model?
rationale: Placement ablations are informative but incremental unless they yield a general principle. Sparse Atari has high variance, so a small game subset may not support broad conclusions.
compute_data_notes: Atari-100k is public, but 8–10 games times three variants, baselines, and seeds with Dreamer is likely more than two to three weeks on one RTX 3080. Montezuma-style games need many seeds.

title: Checkpoint selection inflation.
rationale: The bias is important, easy to communicate, and likely affects published effect sizes, but it follows standard multiple-comparisons logic and may be too narrow for a standalone top-tier paper. A broad audit or integration with evaluation methodology would improve competitiveness.
compute_data_notes: It can reuse existing public run logs or piggyback on local experiments, requiring almost no new training. Analysis is feasible in days on any GPU or CPU.

title: Measure the policy-evaluation lag.
rationale: Turning delayed updates into a measured control variable is a meaningful methodological advance with clear causal tests. The expensive and definition-sensitive Q-policy ground truth, plus possible confounding by extrapolation error, are major weaknesses.
compute_data_notes: Public DMC is sufficient, but repeated critic-to-convergence runs at checkpoints multiply compute; a focused task set is feasible in one to two weeks.

title: Algorithm-induced behavioral bias.
rationale: Deployment-relevant characterization and mechanism ablations suit AAAI, but matched-return comparisons and classifier fingerprints are largely descriptive and sensitive to hyperparameter confounds.
compute_data_notes: Public locomotion/manipulation simulators are available; five algorithms, return matching, and flow-policy implementation make this moderately expensive but feasible in two weeks.

title: Automatic difficulty control for procedural RLVR.
rationale: Adaptive curricula are established, and holding success near 50 percent is a standard heuristic. Broad wins at fixed generation and update compute could be useful, but methodological novelty is limited.
compute_data_notes: Procedural generators avoid data constraints and 0.5B LoRA training is workable. Comparing against a well-tuned fixed mixture across three domains remains several full RL runs.

title: What does legibility cost?
rationale: The monitorability-accuracy frontier is socially relevant and falsifiable, but legibility is hard to define independently of style classifiers and the small-model setting may not exhibit private notation. Human evaluation is also needed for credibility.
compute_data_notes: Procedural public data are easy, but GRPO on 0.5–1.5B models with many penalty strengths is tight on a 10 GB 3080 and human labels are not purely compute-limited.

title: The PPO clip should scale with action dimension.
rationale: The product-ratio argument gives a clear prediction and useful default rule, but dimension-dependent KL scaling is close to established trust-region reasoning and may already be known. Redundant actuators can introduce task changes beyond dimension, so controls are crucial.
compute_data_notes: Public GPU simulators make dimension sweeps cheap, and PPO is straightforward on one 3080. High-DoF tasks may need longer training but the core synthetic test can finish in days.

title: How open-loop is a trained policy?
rationale: A simple intervention could reveal a meaningful hidden property of trained controllers and predict robustness. Frozen-observation action similarity can conflate policy openness with deterministic dynamics or recurrent state, so stronger causal information-use metrics are needed.
compute_data_notes: The study piggybacks on standard public control runs and needs only evaluation interventions; broad seeds and tasks fit in about a week.

title: A scaling law between discount and critic learning rate.
rationale: A predictive tuning law with theory and held-out validation would be broadly useful. The simple hypothesis risks being false or confounded by reward scaling, horizon, optimizer adaptivity, and algorithm-specific target dynamics.
compute_data_notes: Public continuous-control tasks suffice. The grid is large but individual runs are cheap; successive-halving or small tasks make a statistically credible study feasible in one to two weeks.

title: The hidden curriculum in replay-derived datasets.
rationale: Chronology is a neglected, easy-to-test dataset property with practical consequences. Yet standard D4RL releases may not reliably preserve true trajectory-generation chronology, and ordering effects can be optimizer nonstationarity rather than curriculum.
compute_data_notes: D4RL/OGBench and self-generated logs are public or cheap; IQL and TD3+BC runs on MuJoCo fit in about a week.

title: Activation steering for control policies.
rationale: Environment-grounded causal verification makes steering more convincing than correlational interpretability, and ICLR may value the representation angle. SAE novelty is crowded and behavioral feature labeling can become subjective or cherry-picked.
compute_data_notes: Policy training and activation collection in public control tasks are cheap; SAE sweeps and robust feature validation are manageable within two weeks.

title: Horizon generalization benchmark with controlled horizon ratio.
rationale: A controlled benchmark can be useful, but top venues expect durable infrastructure, broad adoption potential, and genuinely surprising findings. Procedural mazes plus block stacking may be too narrow and method implementations may be hard to compare fairly.
compute_data_notes: Procedural mazes are cheap; block-stacking and four methods across ratios and seeds increase engineering and compute. No proprietary data is needed.

title: Critic error tolerance curves.
rationale: Well-controlled diagnostic with interpretable error families, but primarily characterization; competitiveness requires a unifying principle or a method derived from the tolerance map.
compute_data_notes: Public DMC tasks and converged SAC/TD3 checkpoints suffice; actor-only retraining over a distortion grid is inexpensive and 3080-friendly.

title: Do seeds learn the same representation?
rationale: Cross-seed representation convergence is a useful lens on RL instability and could distinguish behavioral versus feature variation. CKA analyses are mature, and differing state visitation makes probe-distribution choice a serious confound.
compute_data_notes: Twenty-plus seeds are inexpensive for gymnax/Craftax but heavier for DMC; public environments and offline CKA computation fit in one to two weeks.

title: Dataset mode count predicts which offline RL method wins.
rationale: Algorithm selection from a dataset statistic is valuable and controlled mixtures offer clean falsification. Estimating conditional behavior-policy mode count is statistically fragile, while five-method rankings need enough tasks and seeds to avoid an overfit meta-result.
compute_data_notes: Public MuJoCo datasets suffice, but generating controlled mixtures and running five methods over many conditions is a substantial two-week 3080 workload.

title: Gradient starvation across action dimensions.
rationale: The mechanism is concrete and relevant to manipulation, but per-coordinate normalization may violate action semantics and resemble routine optimizer engineering. Strong manipulation improvements and causal diagnostics are needed.
compute_data_notes: MyoSuite and Shadow Hand benchmarks are public, but high-DoF manipulation has expensive, high-variance training. A reduced task suite is realistic on one 3080; a convincing broad study may exceed a few weeks.

title: Test-time compute scaling for flow policies in RL.
rationale: Test-time scaling is fashionable, but merely increasing flow steps may not improve a policy trained with fewer discretization steps. The project needs a mechanism enabling refinement, not just a train-by-test grid.
compute_data_notes: DMC and MyoSuite are public and flow policies at this scale fit a 3080. The full train-step by test-step grid with seeds is moderate but feasible.

title: Coarse rewards: quantizing shaped rewards helps.
rationale: Very cheap and falsifiable with an appealing denoising account, but reward discretization is simple and likely task-dependent; venue strength requires a predictive SNR theory that generalizes.
compute_data_notes: Public DMC/Playground, no external data, and tiny implementation overhead make this one of the most feasible ideas on a 3080.

title: The half-life of a transition.
rationale: A useful operational quantity and predictive test, but gradient alignment is only one definition of usefulness and is highly nonstationary. A robust law across algorithms would be needed for a strong paper.
compute_data_notes: All required data are generated in public benchmarks. Per-transition gradients are expensive, but subsampling and projection-based alignment make the study realistic with small agents.

title: A developmental curriculum over degrees of freedom.
rationale: The idea is intuitive and application-friendly, but curricula over action spaces and progressive control are established themes. A fixed proximal-to-distal schedule may not generalize, and strong automatic-curriculum baselines are needed to reach top-tier novelty.
compute_data_notes: MyoSuite and humanoid simulators are public but high-DoF policy training is slower and seed-sensitive. A focused two-task study is possible on a 3080, while broad validation is tight.

title: Does μP hyperparameter transfer survive bootstrapping?
rationale: A careful scaling analysis of bootstrapped learning is methodologically appealing, especially if tau scaling is derived rather than fitted. Novelty risk is high and width-by-learning-rate sweeps can become an empirical parameterization paper with limited RL impact.
compute_data_notes: No private data is needed and networks are small, but dense width, learning-rate, and target-lag sweeps with seeds could consume two weeks.

title: Restart schedules for RL.
rationale: Heavy-tail evidence plus an anytime scheduling result would be useful and unusually actionable. It risks being seen as compute allocation rather than learning methodology, and buffer carryover weakens the classical restart assumptions.
compute_data_notes: The experiment needs hundreds of runs but can use tiny public sparse tasks; one 3080 can parallelize enough seeds in roughly one to two weeks.

title: Activation functions are a hidden pessimism knob in offline RL.
rationale: A clean representation-level hypothesis with useful implications, but an activation sweep risks reading as empirical knob tuning. Competitiveness hinges on a predictive extrapolation theory and held-out validation of penalty selection.
compute_data_notes: D4RL and OGBench are public and avoid online collection. MuJoCo-sized offline training is comfortable on one 3080, enabling broad activation and seed sweeps within two weeks.

title: State-dependent entropy budgeting.
rationale: A statewise target tied to local Q geometry is a plausible algorithmic contribution. However, the direction in the hypothesis is underspecified, Q gradients are noisy and scale-dependent, and prior adaptive entropy work creates novelty pressure.
compute_data_notes: DMC and SAC are public, but stable gradient-sensitive target design and broad tuning may take one to two weeks or more.

title: How many seeds does Atari-100k need now?
rationale: A rigorous leaderboard audit could matter, but six to eight selected games limit claims and reproducing three methods introduces implementation effects. The proposal's compute estimate is incompatible with one RTX 3080.
compute_data_notes: Twenty seeds times 6–8 games times three Atari agents means 360–480 training runs. Even with public code and environments, credible completion on one 3080 in a reasonable paper cycle is unlikely.

title: Exploration order, not exploration magnitude.
rationale: Separating exploration order from bonus magnitude is conceptually clean and can produce falsifiable phase diagrams. The challenge is defining matched-order interventions outside grids without baking in privileged state geometry.
compute_data_notes: Gridworld, MinAtar, and Craftax are public and inexpensive; extensive seeds and controlled reward-location sweeps fit in about a week.

title: Emergent temporal abstraction in flat policies.
rationale: Accessible measurements and a useful hierarchy comparison, but action autocorrelation and compression can reflect task dynamics rather than learned abstraction, weakening causal novelty.
compute_data_notes: Public DMC/Craftax/Playground; sequence statistics are cheap, with hierarchy baselines creating most of the one-week compute burden.

title: Dormant units are fossils.
rationale: The fossil hypothesis is memorable, longitudinally testable, and revival under reversal provides causal leverage. Unit-level interpretations are fragile under distributed representations, and resetting input weights while retaining output weights is not a clean revival test.
compute_data_notes: Craftax and Procgen are public; checkpointing activations and reversal experiments use small networks and fit in about a week.

title: Redundancy reduction as a plasticity regularizer.
rationale: The mechanism is plausible and implementation cheap, but importing Barlow Twins into continual RL is incremental in a crowded regularization space. It needs broad gains and evidence that rank preservation mediates performance.
compute_data_notes: Public Procgen and DMC data are generated online. A model-free auxiliary objective fits a 3080, though broad continual benchmarks and baseline tuning still require many runs.

title: Reward-term decorrelation as a hacking alarm.
rationale: Practical and interpretable application with an online detection target, especially suitable for AAAI; dependence on hand-decomposed rewards and injected exploits limits broad methodological significance.
compute_data_notes: Public robotics simulators suffice, but custom exploit construction and labeled attribution evaluation take engineering; training itself is 3080-feasible.

title: Does RLVR make a model a better in-context explorer?
rationale: A clean and potentially surprising transfer measurement, but it is mostly observational and any change is hard to causally attribute beyond general capability or formatting shifts. Strong matched-SFT controls are essential.
compute_data_notes: Text bandits and gridworlds can be procedurally generated, and evaluation is cheap. Producing the RLVR-tuned checkpoints is the expensive part but a 0.5B LoRA setup is manageable on one 3080.

title: Adaptive group size in GRPO from within-group reward variance.
rationale: The controller and mechanism are simple, but reward-variance-based adaptive sampling is an expected optimization heuristic. Competitiveness depends on a principled compute-saving result and robust gains across tasks.
compute_data_notes: Procedural math is free to generate; QA datasets are public. A 0.5B LoRA setup can fit 10 GB, though larger adaptive groups increase generation memory and wall-clock.

title: Control-frequency transfer: train at 50 Hz, deploy at 20 Hz.
rationale: Practically meaningful with clean continuous-time theory, but characterization alone may be narrow and prior control-frequency robustness work is likely. A principled correction beyond discount rescaling would strengthen it.
compute_data_notes: DMC supports timestep variation and is public. Cross-frequency evaluation is cheap because one trained agent yields many tests; several training frequencies and seeds fit comfortably on one GPU.

title: Which normalization is doing the work in plasticity methods?
rationale: A clean unification could be valuable, but this is primarily an ablation survey in a crowded area. Cross-method differences beyond normalization create attribution problems, and the proposed benchmark breadth dilutes the thesis.
compute_data_notes: All benchmarks are public, but a method-by-normalizer-by-domain-by-seed grid is large. Procgen and continual DMC can make one-3080 turnaround slower than claimed.

title: Exploration waste.
rationale: A ground-truth waste metric could sharpen evaluation of intrinsic motivation, but defining a visit as unnecessary solely from value error is contestable and the proposed gate may use unavailable oracle information. Practical approximations are essential.
compute_data_notes: Small public environments with computable optimal values make the core measurement very cheap; scaling beyond toy state spaces is the main data/engineering issue.

title: Entropy collapse is hysteretic.
rationale: A hysteresis loop is a clean and visually compelling phenomenon with actionable fixes, but entropy collapse is crowded and causal attribution between actor saturation and critic geometry will need careful controls.
compute_data_notes: Public DMC tasks and standard PPO/SAC implementations suffice; coefficient cycles and seeds are feasible in about a week.

title: Interleaved vs blocked domains in RLVR.
rationale: Gradient conflict supplies a principled scheduling signal, but multi-task interference and conflict-aware sampling are crowded topics. RLVR-specific evidence must show behavior beyond direct transfer of supervised multi-task methods.
compute_data_notes: Three procedural public domains are sufficient, but per-domain gradient measurements and several training schedules add compute. Quantized 0.5B LoRA fits, while robust multi-seed comparisons may take several weeks.

title: How linear is a trained policy?
rationale: Clear and potentially useful capacity diagnostic, but novelty and methodological depth are modest given old linear-policy results; a compelling hybrid-capacity method would be needed.
compute_data_notes: Public DMC, Playground, and MyoSuite are available; checkpoint distillation and residual mapping are straightforward on a 3080.

title: Opponent-induced plasticity loss and population size.
rationale: The mechanism is plausible, but population diversity changes learning dynamics in many ways besides plasticity. A population-size sweep risks a correlational result unless plasticity is independently manipulated.
compute_data_notes: MPE and Overcooked are public. Population training multiplies actor count and evaluation cost, though small environments keep a restricted sweep feasible.

title: Transfer the actor, reset the critic.
rationale: The 2x2 component-transfer matrix is useful practice, and contrasting reward versus dynamics shifts is sensible. The recommendation is intuitive folklore and likely has precedents in fine-tuning literature; without a surprising reversal or theory it is below top-conference novelty.
compute_data_notes: DMC and related public task pairs are cheap, with no external data. Four transfer conditions and time-to-threshold curves fit easily on one 3080 in about a week.

title: Weight quantization in closed loop.
rationale: The Lyapunov-based compounding prediction provides more substance than another compression benchmark, and embedded control fits AAAI well. Quantization-aware training is mature and control policy networks are already tiny, limiting broad significance.
compute_data_notes: No external data is needed; post-training quantization, perturbation tests, and noise-aware retraining are inexpensive on public control environments.

title: How many warmup rollouts?
rationale: The result could be practically useful, but fitting a warmup rule is a modest hyperparameter study unless the distribution-gap measure has theoretical or cross-domain validity. Narrow MuJoCo evidence may not generalize.
compute_data_notes: Offline MuJoCo datasets and simulators are public and inexpensive. Sweeping dataset quality, perturbation, and warmup counts is run-heavy but feasible.

title: Depth vs. relabeling horizon: do deep nets need fewer relabeled goals?
rationale: The interaction is clean and cheap, but it is narrower and more incremental than ideas 20 or 21. Two tasks are insufficient for a general claim, and either headline result could explain the outcome without new insight.
compute_data_notes: Two GCRL tasks and a depth-by-horizon grid are feasible on one GPU. Deep configurations may need memory-saving residual blocks, but public data generation is straightforward.

title: How many bits of the advantage does the actor use?
rationale: Extremely clean and useful if sign-only advantages work broadly, but it is a one-line ablation with substantial prior adjacency in clipped, ranked, and sign-based policy gradients. A mechanism or new estimator is needed for a strong paper.
compute_data_notes: Public Procgen and Playground-style tasks are available; matched PPO sweeps are straightforward and fit in several days to a week.

title: Search at test time vs. search at train time, compute-matched.
rationale: Compute-matched evaluation is worthwhile, but adding MCTS to Dreamer is substantial engineering and the comparison to EZ-V2 remains implementation-sensitive. Eight games are too few for a leaderboard-level conclusion.
compute_data_notes: Public Atari data generation is available, but training Dreamer across games and running up to 128 simulations at evaluation is slow. Fair inference-inclusive accounting and MCTS integration make this poor for one 3080.

title: Emergent equivariance.
rationale: The training-time measurement and fine-tuning fragility angle are interesting, especially for representation-focused ICLR. Emergent symmetry is well studied in adjacent supervised and RL work, and the likely result may simply reflect augmentation coverage.
compute_data_notes: Rotational grids and symmetric locomotion tasks are public and cheap; measuring equivariance over checkpoints is straightforward.

title: The n in n-step returns should depend on the transition's age.
rationale: The age-bias hypothesis is testable and could yield a simple method, but age is only a weak proxy for off-policyness and likely loses to importance-ratio or policy-divergence controls. Beating the best fixed n robustly is a high bar.
compute_data_notes: DMC is easy; an Atari-100k subset and Monte Carlo target estimates add runtime and variance but remain plausible in one to two weeks on a 3080.

title: Do sample-efficient learners converge to worse optima?
rationale: The question challenges common reporting practice and could produce useful evidence, but 'to convergence' is hard to define and endpoint differences may reflect tuning or objective details. The proposal is expensive and mainly empirical.
compute_data_notes: Algorithms and environments are public, but six tasks, five methods, multiple seeds, and genuinely long runs are demanding on one 3080. A smaller study is feasible but less convincing.

title: The deterministic-evaluation gap as a diagnostic.
rationale: A virtually free diagnostic with predictive value would improve evaluation practice, but the stated sign interpretations are not uniquely implied and distribution semantics differ across policy families. It is stronger as one component of a broader diagnostics paper.
compute_data_notes: Uses existing public-task checkpoints and adds only sampled-versus-mean evaluations; compute and data feasibility are excellent.

title: Learning-path imitation.
rationale: The inversion of expert-only cloning is practical and the source-window prediction adds a useful hypothesis. Early-buffer benefits may reduce to generic coverage or replay pretraining, leaving modest novelty unless the state-distribution predictor generalizes.
compute_data_notes: Self-generated buffers in public DMC/Craftax are easy to obtain; windowed BC and fine-tuning sweeps fit in about a week.

title: Value-preserving observation compression for replay.
rationale: A sensible task-aware codec with practical memory benefits, but value-aware representation learning and replay compression are mature areas. Preserving the current critic may erase information needed by future critics, creating a key nonstationarity issue.
compute_data_notes: Atari-100k and pixel DMC are public, but online codec training and repeated pixel-agent runs are moderately expensive and 10 GB memory is tight. A focused game subset is feasible in two to three weeks.

title: Bursty vs steady updates at fixed UTD.
rationale: The temporal arrangement of updates is underreported and the matched-UTD ablation is clean. It is still a schedule study with likely strong task dependence, so a mechanistic predictor of optimal burst length is needed.
compute_data_notes: DMC and Playground are public; the burst-by-UTD grid is moderately large but GPU-parallel and feasible in about a week.

title: Reward-term equalization.
rationale: More principled than reward dropout and directly addresses hand tuning, but per-term actor-gradient attribution is ambiguous because returns combine over time and terms can encode different priorities. Application value may exceed foundational novelty.
compute_data_notes: Public decomposed-reward locomotion tasks are available. Computing separate per-term gradient statistics increases backward-pass cost but remains feasible on one GPU with a modest task suite.

title: Should the actor see the critic's uncertainty?
rationale: Quantile-aware actor objectives are well explored under distributional and risk-sensitive RL, so the novelty claim is weak. A focused discovery about exploration under epistemic versus aleatoric uncertainty could improve it.
compute_data_notes: DMC and risk-sensitive control tasks are public and inexpensive. Existing distributional critics make implementation easy on one GPU.

title: Churn hotspots are bottleneck states.
rationale: Elegant, cheap, and visually interpretable, with a useful hierarchy application. The link can be tautological because uncertain decision states naturally churn, and graph bottleneck methods provide strong established baselines.
compute_data_notes: Four Rooms, MiniGrid, and Craftax are public and tiny. Checkpoint logging, heatmaps, and hierarchical-agent tests are easily completed on one 3080 within a week.

title: Tanh saturation as a failure mode.
rationale: The diagnostic is concrete and deployment-relevant, but tanh saturation and alternative action distributions are well known. Correlation with stalls is insufficient; convincing causal interventions and strong distributional baselines are required.
compute_data_notes: DMC and Playground are cheap; MyoSuite broadens evidence but increases setup and runtime. One to two weeks is realistic.

title: Initialization is an exploration hyperparameter.
rationale: A crisp, cheap factorial study could expose a widely overlooked interaction, but optimistic initialization is old and the proposed sign-based rule may look like benchmark-specific tuning unless supported by theory and broad tasks.
compute_data_notes: Fully public simulators and tiny networks; many seeds and factorial sweeps fit comfortably on a 3080 in about a week.

title: Optimizer momentum carries gradients from a dead policy.
rationale: Extremely clean and cheap, with a plausible mechanism, but likely viewed as an optimizer ablation unless supported by a derivation of effective trust-region distortion and consistent cross-task effects.
compute_data_notes: PPO benchmarks are public, require no fixed dataset, and momentum resets are trivial to implement. Dozens of runs on small GPU-native tasks can be completed in days on one 3080.

title: Flow-policy noise as a temporally correlated exploration variable.
rationale: A natural extension of structured exploration to flow policies and well aligned with ICLR, but close to latent-variable, parameter-noise, and temporally coherent exploration work. It needs benefits uniquely attributable to multimodal flow structure.
compute_data_notes: DMC and maze tasks are public. Small flow policies fit readily, though implementing a stable online flow-policy baseline is more work than the noise variants themselves.

title: How specialization scales with team size.
rationale: The scaling question is clear and may explain parameter-sharing behavior, but the claimed rise-then-collapse is speculative and specialization metrics are representation- and permutation-sensitive. Without a new predictive theory it is mostly characterization.
compute_data_notes: Public JaxMARL environments support fast parallel sweeps; N up to 32 with multiple parameterizations and seeds remains feasible in one to two weeks.

title: Paraphrase groups.
rationale: The group construction directly targets prompt robustness and is easy to understand, but it resembles standard augmentation/consistency training and synthetic paraphrase quality can dominate results. Lower variance is not guaranteed because prompts change task difficulty.
compute_data_notes: Template paraphrases avoid proprietary APIs and the rollout count is matched; a focused 0.5B LoRA study is feasible in roughly a week.

title: Role adapters: low-rank per-agent deltas on a shared policy.
rationale: The method is simple and rank offers an interpretable heterogeneity axis, but applying LoRA to MARL is an obvious transfer with likely recent precedents. Strong wins over shared-plus-ID and parameter-matched multi-head baselines are necessary.
compute_data_notes: JaxMARL data are generated online and networks are tiny; rank sweeps should finish within a week on one GPU.

title: Deep critics and seed variance.
rationale: Statistical power analysis is useful, but critic size versus variance alone is narrow and likely benchmark-dependent. Top-tier strength requires a general variance mechanism or evaluation recommendation that survives algorithms and environments.
compute_data_notes: Gymnax and Craftax are public and GPU-vectorized; 50–100 seeds are realistic because tasks and networks are small. Multiple independent seed batches should verify variance estimates.

title: A minimal task subset for continuous control.
rationale: Benchmark compression is useful and has a clear validation criterion, but Atari-5 makes the approach incremental and published scores are heterogeneous. Fifteen methods across three suites exceed the claimed collection ease if results must be standardized.
compute_data_notes: Published tables are public but incomplete and noncomparable; rerunning enough methods and tasks with seeds is likely infeasible on one 3080 in one week.

title: How many parameters does adaptation need?
rationale: Rank as an adaptation-distance measure is neat and cheap, but LoRA for control adaptation is an obvious, likely published direction and raw rank is architecture-dependent. The scalar-shift rank-1 claim needs theory to escape an incremental study.
compute_data_notes: Public DMC/Playground policies are small, and LoRA rank-by-shift sweeps are comfortably feasible within a week.

title: Jacobian distillation for RL (not just BC) policies.
rationale: This is a direct technique transfer with a clear experiment but limited independent novelty. A credible top-tier paper would need an RL-specific phenomenon involving the critic, not just positive results on manipulation.
compute_data_notes: CRL/HIQL and public manipulation tasks are modest. Jacobian computation adds memory and runtime but should fit small networks on a 3080.

title: Residual gradients, revisited under modern architecture.
rationale: A worthwhile reassessment with a clear answer, but the novelty is primarily updating an old comparison. It becomes competitive only if modern architecture reveals a robust regime and the paper explains why.
compute_data_notes: DMC and Atari-100k are public. Double-sampled residual methods may require simulator branching or paired transitions; UTD-by-architecture grids are feasible but costly enough to require a narrow benchmark.

title: Kill the run early: predicting final return from the first 5%.
rationale: Useful tooling with an honest regret metric, but learning-curve extrapolation and early stopping are crowded. Novel RL features help only if they generalize across tasks and beat strong curve-based methods.
compute_data_notes: No proprietary data are needed, but 500-plus labeled runs require completing enough full runs to know final return. Tiny public tasks make this possible, though the resulting scale may weaken relevance to larger RL.

title: Heterogeneous-temperature groups.
rationale: This is a plausible GRPO improvement with a clean variance measurement, but temperature mixing is a narrow sampling heuristic and comparison to adaptive sampling and importance correction is essential. The proposed baseline may also be biased across temperatures.
compute_data_notes: No proprietary data is needed, but matched-rollout RLVR across domains and schedules is still a sizeable one-GPU experiment.

title: Detecting reward hacking from the shape of the return distribution.
rationale: Important application goal and a clear held-out-exploit test, but return-distribution shape alone is unlikely to identify semantic hacking reliably. Constructing diverse labeled exploits without leakage is the dominant scientific challenge.
compute_data_notes: Some public benchmark bugs exist, but a standardized public exploit corpus does not. Injecting enough varied exploits and legitimate abrupt improvements is labor intensive; model training itself is cheap.

title: The observation normalizer is a hidden nonstationarity.
rationale: This is a useful reproducibility diagnostic with a clear intervention, but the likely contribution is infrastructural and freezing normalizers is already common practice. It needs surprisingly large effects across algorithms to clear a top-tier bar.
compute_data_notes: All environments and baselines are public; instrumentation and ablations are cheap and should complete within days.

title: Hot-swapping the reward function mid-training.
rationale: Highly practical for reward iteration and a good AAAI application story, but buffer reward relabeling is straightforward and closely related to relabeling and transfer methods. Predicting recovery cost must be unusually accurate to supply research novelty.
compute_data_notes: Public GPU control tasks with decomposed rewards make all variants cheap; one week is ample on a 3080.

title: Spaced repetition for RLVR.
rationale: A plausible curriculum heuristic with a clean retention test, but borrowing SM-2 is conceptually incremental and benefits may reduce to ordinary prioritized sampling. A learned forgetting model or theory would be needed for higher competitiveness.
compute_data_notes: Procedural domains avoid proprietary data and can generate unlimited examples. One 0.5B LoRA run fits with memory-saving methods, but multiple curricula and seeds make wall-clock substantial on a 3080.

title: Where the regularizer enters: target or actor.
rationale: The factorial is useful and clean, but the ingredients and partial ablations already exist, so it looks more like careful empirical clarification than a new learning principle. A surprising interaction or derived decoupled algorithm is needed for a top-tier claim.
compute_data_notes: All environments and algorithms are public, and eight configurations are cheap. One 3080 can run the study in days to a week with a restricted task suite.

title: Learned observation masks as sensor selection.
rationale: Useful for robust control but close to feature selection, L0 regularization, attention, and sensor dropout. The research contribution needs a specifically RL-dependent phenomenon or a strong deployment result.
compute_data_notes: Public proprioceptive control suites expose sensor vectors and train cheaply. Learned masks and corruption tests are straightforward on a 3080.

title: How many parallel environments is too many?
rationale: Useful practitioner guidance, but the stated mechanism confounds batch freshness, update ratio, rollout length, and optimization. Without a general predictive law it is mostly a benchmark sweep.
compute_data_notes: Public GPU-native environments make the grid practical, but a 10 GB 3080 limits the upper environment counts. Matched-step and matched-wall-clock experiments remain feasible on modest tasks.

title: Reward dropout.
rationale: Simple and potentially useful, especially for robotics applications, but it is an analogy-driven regularizer with weak methodological depth. Strong robustness and sparse-success gains across reward structures are needed.
compute_data_notes: Public GPU-native locomotion tasks expose decomposed rewards and train quickly. A dropout sweep and sparse-metric evaluation are straightforward on one 3080.

title: Denoising steps as temperature.
rationale: The hypothesis is easy to falsify but technically questionable: solver step count primarily changes approximation error, not a monotonic distribution temperature. Even if effective, it may look like a narrow heuristic.
compute_data_notes: Public DMC tasks are sufficient and small flow or diffusion policies fit on one 3080. Step-count sweeps are computationally manageable, although 16-step action sampling reduces throughput.

title: Deduplicating replay in GPU-native environments.
rationale: Practical and easy to test, but likely a systems optimization rather than a research contribution unless deduplication reveals a surprising statistical law or changes learning substantially at matched wall-clock.
compute_data_notes: GPU-native environments are public and latent hashing is affordable. Memory savings are easy to measure on a 3080, although the claimed update-cost reduction needs a careful implementation.
